subject: CSC
label: Grade 11 Science
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 11 Science Computer science, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Python programming: control flow and strings
modules.outcome: write programs with decisions and loops
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Python programming: control flow and strings', taught in a way that is with exam-style questions and written reasoning. The target is clear: write programs with decisions and loops. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: See it: watch or try the skill in 'Python programming: control flow and strings' on a teacher screen or a safe device.
Name the parts: write the key words and what each part does.
Use it: write programs with decisions and loops. Save your work in a named file or folder.
Test and fix: run it, find one fault, correct it, and note what you changed.
modules.example: Solved: name = 'Sara'; total = 0; for n in [3, 5, 7]: total = total + n; print(name, total) prints Sara 15. Trace each line to check. Method: Model run for 'Python programming: control flow and strings'. Goal in one sentence. Plan: list the steps in order before touching the device. Do: follow the plan, saving after each step. Test: try normal input and one unusual input. Fix: change one thing and test again. Share: show a partner and explain it. What a good answer looks like: it works for normal input, steps match the plan, and the learner can explain each part. Online safety rules apply at all times.
modules.activity: About 40 to 50 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a timed paper and an error log.
modules.standard: Write programs with decisions and loops: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.
